components.note: 广 (building) — the older sense of 废 was a building falling into ruin, hence 'discarded'
发 (fā) gives the sound — shares the vowel with fèi

example.pinyin: Zhè tái jiù diànnǎo yǐjīng fèi le.
example.english: This old computer is already useless.
example.fact: 废 is usually seen inside compounds such as 废话 (pointless talk), 废物 (waste, or a useless person) and 废除 (to abolish). Used alone as an adjective it is blunt and colloquial, like saying something is 'dead' or 'junk'.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — a shed or roof
林 (grove) — rows of hemp stalks, here drying under the shed

example.pinyin: Wǒ de tuǐ má le.
example.english: My leg has gone numb.
example.fact: 麻 covers hemp and also 'numb, tingling', as when a limb falls asleep. It sits inside very common words such as 麻烦 (trouble), 麻将 (mahjong) and 麻辣 (numbing-and-spicy, the Sichuan flavour).

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — an old money radical, tying 赖 to profit, debt and reliance
剌 (là) gives the sound — very close to lài

example.pinyin: Bié lài wǒ, bú shì wǒ nòng huài de.
example.english: Don't blame me, I'm not the one who broke it.
example.fact: 赖 shows up in 赖账 (to refuse to pay a debt), 无赖 (rogue) and 依赖 (to depend on). In speech, 赖 someone means to pin the blame on them unfairly, and 赖在某处 means to hang around and refuse to leave.

components.note: 目 (eye) — watching over someone is the core of supervising
叔 (shū) gives a loose sound hint — the vowel matches dū but the initial has drifted

example.hanzi: 老师督促我们每天复习。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī dūcù wǒmen měitiān fùxí.
example.english: The teacher urges us to review every day.
example.fact: 督 is a bound form found in 督促 (to urge), 监督 (to supervise) and 总督 (governor-general). It also appears in 基督, the Chinese rendering of 'Christ', so 基督教 means Christianity.

components.note: 乚 (a hooked stroke) — marks a bent, hidden shape in the character
孚 (fú) is the main body of the character and offers only a distant sound hint

example.pinyin: Yīng'ér zuì hǎo hē mǔrǔ.
example.english: Babies are best fed breast milk.
example.fact: 乳 is the formal word for milk: 乳制品 (dairy products), 乳酸 (lactic acid), 乳房 (breast). In daily speech people say 牛奶 for a glass of cow's milk, reserving 乳 for written, technical or medical contexts.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, fitting a particle used at the end of spoken sentences
贝 (bèi) gives the sound — nearly identical to bei

example.pinyin: Bù huì jiù xué bei.
example.english: If you can't do it, just learn it, then.
example.fact: Sentence-final 呗 (bei) conveys that something is obvious or no big deal, often with a hint of 'so what?'. It is chatty and a bit casual, unlike 吧, which softens a suggestion. The original reading bài is the 'chant' in 梵呗, Buddhist chanting.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — itching is a bodily discomfort, so it sits under the sickness radical
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — only the tone differs from yǎng

example.pinyin: Wǒ de bèi hěn yǎng.
example.english: My back is very itchy.
example.fact: 痒 combines with other words: 发痒 (to itch), 挠痒 (to scratch an itch), and 怕痒 (to be ticklish). 手痒 literally 'hands itch' means you are itching to try or join in, such as playing a game.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — holding is something done with the hand
寺 (sì) is a loose sound hint; the pronunciation has shifted over time

example.pinyin: Qǐng chí piào rù chǎng.
example.english: Please enter with your ticket in hand.
example.fact: 持 rarely stands alone in conversation, but it is the core of many everyday words: 支持 (support), 坚持 (persist), 保持 (keep, maintain) and 持续 (continue). On signs, 持 + object means 'holding/with', as in 持证 (holding a pass).

components.note: A left-hand 彳 (step) beside a complex right half; the structure is old and its original picture is debated, so it is best learned as a whole.

example.pinyin: Tā wēixiào zhe diǎn le diǎn tóu.
example.english: She nodded with a slight smile.
example.fact: 微 means tiny or slight and works as a prefix: 微笑 (smile), 微波炉 (microwave oven), 微信 (WeChat, literally 'micro-message') and 微博 (microblog). 微 is also the 'micro-' of 微米 (micrometre).

components.note: 氵 (water) — thickness is first of all a quality of liquids
农 (nóng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài nóng le.
example.english: This coffee is too strong.
example.fact: 浓 describes liquids, smells, colours and even feelings: 浓茶 (strong tea), 浓烟 (thick smoke), 浓厚 (strong, as in interest) and 浓情蜜意 (deep affection). Its opposite is 淡 (weak, light).

components.note: 心 (heart) — anger is an emotion, so it sits over the heart
奴 (nú) gives the sound — differs only in tone

example.pinyin: Tā nùqì chōngchōng de zǒu le.
example.english: He left in a towering rage.
example.fact: 怒 is stronger and more literary than 生气: 发怒 (fly into a rage), 愤怒 (indignant), 怒火 (flames of anger). It also describes flowers in 怒放, 'blooming with abandon'.

components.note: 匚 (open frame) — outlines the L-shaped body of a carpenter's square, the tool the older form 巨 stood for

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè jùdà de jīngxǐ.
example.english: This is a huge surprise.
example.fact: 巨 mostly appears in compounds: 巨大 (enormous), 巨人 (giant), 巨星 (superstar) and 巨额 (a huge sum). Young people also use it as a casual intensifier, as in 巨好吃 'insanely tasty'.

components.note: 方 (square) — a stand-in for the old banner radical, picturing a flag on a pole
其 (qí) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Nà miàn qí shì hóngsè de.
example.english: That flag is red.
example.fact: The measure word for flags is 面 (miàn): 一面旗. 旗 also appears in 旗袍 (qipao), literally 'banner robe', named after the Manchu 'banner' (旗) people who wore the original form.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the body-part radical, showing 肾 is an organ

example.pinyin: Tā de shèn bù tài hǎo.
example.english: His kidneys aren't in great shape.
example.fact: In everyday talk 肾 is also a cultural term: traditional Chinese medicine treats the kidney as the store of vitality, so 肾虚 ('kidney deficiency') is a very common worry. As a food ingredient, kidneys are often called 腰子.

components.note: 足 (foot) — jumping is something the feet do
崩 (bēng) gives the sound — nearly identical to bèng

example.hanzi: 孩子们在草地上又蹦又跳。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài cǎodì shang yòu bèng yòu tiào.
example.english: The kids are bouncing and jumping about on the grass.
example.fact: 蹦 describes springy hopping with both feet: 蹦蹦跳跳 (skipping about) and 蹦极 (bungee jumping, phonetic-plus-sense). 蹦迪 is slang for going clubbing.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — belly is a body part
土 (tǔ) offers a loose sound hint for dù

example.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi è le.
example.english: I'm hungry.
example.fact: Standing alone, 肚 normally means the belly, read dù, and 肚子 is the colloquial word for stomach or belly (我肚子疼 'my stomach hurts'). Read dǔ it means tripe, as in 爆肚, a Beijing dish.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a source is where water starts
原 (yuán) gives the sound, and was itself the earlier word for 'source'; 源 added water to it

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de yuántóu zài shān lǐ.
example.english: The source of this river is in the mountains.
example.fact: 源 appears in 资源 (resources), 来源 (source), 电源 (power supply), 源头 (headwaters) and 开源 (open source). It is also a surname.

components.note: 氵 (water) — bathing involves water
谷 (gǔ) offers a loose sound hint for yù

example.pinyin: Tā zài yùshì lǐ chànggē.
example.english: He is singing in the bathroom.
example.fact: 浴 is a formal, written word for bathing: 浴室 (bathroom), 浴缸 (bathtub), 淋浴 (shower), 沐浴 (to bathe). In ordinary speech 洗澡 is the usual verb, while 浴 sits in nouns and signage.

components.note: 力 (strength) — vigour and energy
孛 (bó) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì shēngjī bóbó.
example.english: This city is full of vitality.
example.fact: 勃 is often doubled or placed in set phrases: 生机勃勃 (full of vitality), 野心勃勃 (full of ambition), 兴致勃勃 (in high spirits) and 勃然大怒 (flaring up in anger).

components.note: A simplified form of 壽, whose top was an altered 老 (old); the modern shape (丰 over 寸) keeps only a rough outline, so learn it as a whole.

example.hanzi: 祝您生日快乐，健康长寿！
example.pinyin: Zhù nín shēngrì kuàilè, jiànkāng chángshòu!
example.english: Happy birthday, and wishing you good health and a long life!
example.fact: 寿 is central to birthday culture for the elderly: 寿桃 (longevity peach buns), 寿面 (long noodles) and 做寿 (hold a birthday banquet). It also appears in 寿命 (lifespan) and, borrowed from Japanese, 寿司 (sushi).

components.note: 足 (foot) — kneeling bends the legs
危 (wēi) offers a loose sound hint for guì

example.pinyin: Tā guì zài dì shang qiú tā yuánliàng.
example.english: He knelt on the ground, begging her forgiveness.
example.fact: 跪 is used in 下跪 (to kneel down), 跪拜 (to bow on one's knees) and 磕头 scenes in historical dramas. In modern slang, 跪了 means 'I'm done for / I give up', as if collapsing on one's knees.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — cooking over heat
前 (qián) gives the sound — close, differing mainly in the initial

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang jiān le liǎng gè dàn.
example.english: This morning I fried two eggs.
example.fact: 煎 means pan-frying in a thin layer of oil, unlike 炸 (deep-frying) and 炒 (stir-frying). Pot-stickers and eggs are 煎ed. It also means to simmer herbal medicine: 煎药.

components.note: 土 (earth) — the base meaning is something that can bear weight, like ground
甚 (shèn, very) — a large amount, hinting at capacity and endurance

example.pinyin: Tā lèi de píbèi bùkān.
example.english: He is utterly exhausted.
example.fact: 堪 is literary. The pattern 不堪 means 'unbearably…', as in 疲惫不堪 (exhausted) or 不堪入耳 (unbearable to hear). 堪称 means 'can be called', as in 堪称完美 (can be called perfect).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — coaxing is done with words
共 (gòng) offers a loose sound hint for hǒng

example.pinyin: Māma zài hǒng bǎobao shuìjiào.
example.english: Mum is soothing the baby to sleep.
example.fact: 哄 has three readings: hǒng (coax or fool, as in 哄孩子, 哄女朋友 'sweet-talk your girlfriend'), hōng (a roar of laughter, 哄堂大笑) and hòng (uproar, 起哄 'to heckle').

components.note: 犭 (dog) — dogs were the hunter's partners
昔 (xī) offers a loose sound hint for liè

example.pinyin: Tā yǐ dǎliè wéi shēng.
example.english: He makes a living by hunting.
example.fact: 猎 shows up in 打猎 (to hunt), 猎人 (hunter), 猎物 (prey) and 猎奇 (to seek novelty). 猎头 is the modern term for a headhunter, a recruiter.

components.note: 玨 (paired jade) — suggests jewel-like strings or ornament on the instrument
必 (bì) offers only a distant sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā lěng de sèsè fādǒu.
example.english: He was shivering with cold.
example.fact: In 瑟瑟 the word describes a rustling or trembling, as in 秋风瑟瑟 or 瑟瑟发抖. By itself 瑟 is an ancient 25-string zither; the famous pairing 琴瑟 is a poetic symbol of a harmonious marriage.

components.note: A mouth-shaped frame with a stroke inside, picturing something held in the mouth and tasted — the sense of sweetness.

example.pinyin: Tā gānyuàn wèi nǐ fùchū.
example.english: He is willing to give for you.
example.fact: 甘 is a literary word for sweet and for willingness: 甘心 (resigned willingly), 甘甜 (sweet), 同甘共苦 (share joys and hardships). Gān is also a short name for Gansu province (甘肃).

components.note: 刂 (knife) — peeling is cutting off a layer
录 (lù) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bāo yí gè chéngzi.
example.english: Please peel an orange for me.
example.fact: 剥 has two readings: bāo is the colloquial 'peel, shell' (剥虾 shell prawns); bō is literary, found in 剥削 (exploit) and 剥夺 (deprive).

components.note: 亻 (person) — manners and bearing are human
义 (yì) gives the sound — differs only in the initial

example.pinyin: Zhège yíshì hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: This ceremony is very important.
example.fact: 仪 is a bound form: 仪式 (ceremony), 礼仪 (etiquette), 仪器 (instrument), 仪表 (appearance; also a gauge). Anything named 某某仪 is typically a measuring device, as in 地球仪 (globe).

components.note: 犭 (animal) — marks an animal
侯 (hóu) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō hóuzi.
example.english: There are lots of monkeys at the zoo.
example.fact: The monkey is the ninth zodiac animal (猴年 = year of the monkey) and the star of Journey to the West as 美猴王, the Monkey King. The measure word is 只.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — smoke comes from fire

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng ròu shì yòng yān xūn de.
example.english: This meat is smoked.
example.fact: 熏 covers smoking food (熏肉, 熏鱼), fumigating (熏蚊子) and being irritated by smoke. In 熏陶 (to influence gradually) it may also be written 薰陶.

components.note: 酋 (wine vessel) — the offering placed in the vessel
寸 (hand) — presenting the offering with the hand

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnzhòng lǎorén.
example.english: We should respect older people.
example.fact: 尊 gives 尊敬 (respect people, admiration) and 尊重 (respect opinions, rights). It is also the measure word for statues and cannons (一尊佛像), and appears in 尊称 (honorific).

components.note: 冫 (ice) — stands in for the water radical in the older form 湊, picturing water flowing together
奏 (zòu) gives the sound — a near match

example.hanzi: 大家凑钱买了一个蛋糕。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā còu qián mǎi le yí gè dàngāo.
example.english: Everyone chipped in to buy a cake.
example.fact: 凑 is handy in colloquial phrases: 凑钱 (chip in), 凑合 (make do), 凑热闹 (join in the fun) and 凑巧 (by coincidence).

components.note: 土 (earth) — earthen walls
保 (bǎo, protect) — defence; it also gives the sound

example.hanzi: 山上有一座古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: Shān shang yǒu yí zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: There is an ancient castle on the mountain.
example.fact: 堡 appears in 城堡 (castle), 堡垒 (stronghold) and 汉堡 (hamburger). In some northern place names it is read bǔ or pù.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — blows and fighting
贝 (bèi) gives the sound — close to bài

example.hanzi: 我们队以一分之差败给了对手。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì yǐ yì fēn zhī chā bài gěi le duìshǒu.
example.english: Our team lost to the opponent by one point.
example.fact: 败 pairs with 胜 (win): 胜败. 打败 means to beat, 失败 means to fail. 败家 means to squander the family fortune, and 败家子 is a spendthrift.

components.note: 彐 (hand) — a hand grasping
禾 (grain) — two stalks held together, the image of holding two things at once

example.pinyin: Tā jiānrèn liǎng gè zhíwù.
example.english: He holds two posts at once.
example.fact: 兼 means doing two things at once: 兼职 (part-time job), 兼顾 (to look after both), 兼容 (compatible), 兼职 on a CV. It is a formal word.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a fruit tree
兆 (zhào) offers a loose sound hint for táo

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī táozi.
example.english: I love eating peaches the most.
example.fact: The peach is a symbol of longevity: 寿桃 are peach-shaped buns for birthdays. 桃花运 means romantic luck, and 桃花源 is a famous utopia from Tao Yuanming.

components.note: 氵 (water) — ice melting and draining away
肖 (xiào) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā de nùqì jiànjiàn xiāo le.
example.english: His anger gradually faded.
example.fact: 消 is the heart of 消息 (news), 消失 (vanish), 消费 (consume), 消化 (digest) and 取消 (cancel). On its own, it means to subside, as in 肿消了, 'the swelling went down'.

components.note: 日 (sun) — light that makes things visible
业 (yè) is a simplified stand-in for the old right-hand side, not a real sound hint

example.hanzi: 这件衣服显得你很年轻。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu xiǎnde nǐ hěn niánqīng.
example.english: This outfit makes you look young.
example.fact: 显得 means 'to look, to seem' and is extremely common. 显然 is 'obviously', 显示 is 'to display', and 明显 is 'clear'.

components.note: 木 (wood) — raw, unworked timber
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound — close to pǔ

example.pinyin: Tā chuān de hěn pǔsù.
example.english: She dresses very simply.
example.fact: 朴 originally meant uncut wood, which explains 朴素 (simple), 朴实 (down-to-earth) and 质朴 (unaffected). It is also a surname, read Piáo (as in Korean Park).

components.note: 玨 (paired jade) — suggests the instrument's strings
今 (jīn) offers a loose sound hint for qín

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang tán gāngqín.
example.english: She plays the piano every evening.
example.fact: 琴 is the general word for stringed and keyboard instruments: 钢琴 (piano), 小提琴 (violin), 古琴 (guqin). The verbs differ: 弹 for plucked or keyboard instruments, 拉 for bowed ones (拉小提琴).

components.note: 钅 (metal) — money and coinage
旁 (páng) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū mài shí yīngbàng.
example.english: This book costs ten pounds.
example.fact: 镑 appears essentially in 英镑 (pound sterling). The weight 'pound' is written 磅, with a stone radical instead of metal.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — small creatures with many legs
下 (xià) gives the sound — a close match

example.pinyin: Zhè pán xiā hěn xīnxiān.
example.english: This plate of shrimp is very fresh.
example.fact: 虾 is the shrimp; 龙虾 is a lobster, 小龙虾 is crayfish (a hugely popular summer street food), and 虾米 is dried shrimp.

components.note: Now stands for 薑 (ginger) as a simplification; the 羊-over-女 shape is actually an older, separate surname character.

example.hanzi: 做鱼的时候要放一点姜。
example.pinyin: Zuò yú de shíhou yào fàng yìdiǎn jiāng.
example.english: When cooking fish you need to add a little ginger.
example.fact: 姜 is also a common surname. The proverb 姜还是老的辣 ('old ginger is the spiciest') means experience beats youth.

components.note: 豕 (pig) — the old sense referred to a bristly boar
高 (gāo) offers a loose sound hint for háo

example.hanzi: 我为我的国家感到自豪。
example.pinyin: Wǒ wèi wǒ de guójiā gǎndào zìháo.
example.english: I feel proud of my country.
example.fact: 豪 is found in 自豪 (proud), 豪华 (luxurious), 豪爽 (hearty and open) and 豪言壮语 (grand words). 土豪 (rich, showy person) became a joke term in the 2010s.

components.note: An old character whose exact picture is uncertain: a roof-like top over a 口 mouth. It is best learned as a unit.

example.pinyin: Shìqing shàng wèi jiéshù.
example.english: The matter is not yet over.
example.fact: 尚 is literary. 尚未 means 'not yet' (formal, often in news), 时尚 is 'fashion' and 高尚 is 'noble'. 和尚 (Buddhist monk) is read héshang with a neutral tone.

components.note: A structure of 广 over 肀 and 口 whose old meaning 'big talk' is debated, so it is best learned as a whole.

example.pinyin: Tángcháo de shīgē hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: Tang dynasty poetry is very famous.
example.fact: 唐 (618-907) is seen as a golden age: 唐诗 (Tang poetry), 唐三彩 (Tang tricolour pottery). Overseas, 唐人街 (Chinatown) means 'Tang people's street', and 唐 is a surname.

components.note: 土 (earth) — levelling ground so that it is even
匀 (yún) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Zhè pī huò de zhìliàng jūn hégé.
example.english: The quality of this batch of goods is all up to standard.
example.fact: 均 as an adverb means 'all, without exception' and is formal: 均可 (all are acceptable). It is the core of 平均 (average) and 均匀 (even, uniform).

components.note: 贝 (shell) — the old form 質 had it, relating to value and exchange

example.hanzi: 这家店的东西质量很好。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
example.english: The goods in this shop are of good quality.
example.fact: 质 is a bound form seen in 质量 (quality; also 'mass' in physics), 品质 (character), 物质 (matter), 本质 (essence) and 质问 (to question sharply).

components.note: 氵 (water) — floating happens on water
孚 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Mùtou néng fú zài shuǐ shang.
example.english: Wood can float on water.
example.fact: 浮 means floating (浮在水上) and, figuratively, shallow or restless: 浮躁 (impatient), 浮华 (flashy), 浮云 (fleeting clouds, an image of worldly things).
